results.title: Controlled Vocabulary & Free-Text - Advanced Search Strategies - Subject and Course Guides at University of Illinois at Chicago
results.content: ### Search UIC Library Collections. ### Search UIC Library Website. 5. Controlled Vocabulary & Free-Text. ## Controlled Vocabulary/Free-text/Floating Subheadings for Each Database:. Most databases use**Medical Subject Headings (MeSH)** terms for controlled vocabulary searching. Official MeSH terms provide a way to search all articles for a topic by using one phrase. MeSH terms are automatically exploded by PubMed, which means more specific terms listed underneath your search term will be included in your search. Floating subheadings allow subheadings to be searched unattached to a specific term. A floating subheading example is adding "standard" to "exercise therapy." Results will include any subject heading where the pairing is possible, which can include irrelevant sources. | **Databases** | **Controlled Vocabulary** | **Free-text** | **Floating Subheadings** |. | **Cochrane** | MeSH | exercise:ti,ab,kw | [mh/TH]  will not be exploded |. | **APA PsycINFO** | ProQuest Thesaurus & MeSH | TI,AB,IF("exercise therapy") | N/A |. | **Scopus** | Free-text only | TITLE-ABS-KEY ("exercise therapy") | N/A |.

results.title: Emtree (Embase subject headings) - Embase - LibGuides at University of Toledo Libraries
results.content: ## Embase Guides for Subject Headings and Indexing. **Emtree is a list of subject headings unique to Embase**. * Emtree subject headings will retrieve most associated synonyms for the entered term. * The full text of journal articles are indexed in Embase, not just title and abstract as in PubMed. **MeSH (Medical Subject Headings) are used to index articles and other published information in PubMed/Medline. MeSH terms are used in much the same way as Emtree - to include synonyms and find associated broader and narrower terms.**. | Fewer medical device terms | More medical device terms, including trade name  indexing; medical device search form and device  subheadings thatshow relationships to related terms  (e.g adverse device events, device comparison,  device economics) |. 11 of Embase Indexing Guide 2015. **Automatic indexing for selected articles was introduced into Embase in 2009.**. Automatically indexed articles are indexed with Emtree terms, selected by an algorithm which is applied to the text of titles, abstracts and author keywords.

Vol. 110 No. 1 (2022): January 2022/ MeSH and text-word search strategies: precision, recall, and their implications for library instruction DeMars Health Sciences Librarian, California State University, Long Beach, Long Beach, CA * Carol Perruso Associate Librarian, California State University, Long Beach, Long Beach, CA Precision, Recall, MeSH, MeSH Instruction, Relevant Recall Method Objective: This study compared the recall and precision of MeSH-term versus text-word searching to better understand psychosocial MeSH terms and to provide guidance on whether to include both strategies in an information literacy session or how much time should be spent on teaching each search strategy. We compared resources discussing psychosocial aspects of children and adolescents living with type 1 diabetes using two search strategies: text-word strategy versus MeSH-term strategy. Results:Using the 1,521 relevant articles, we found that the text-word search strategy had 54% recall, while the MeSH-term strategy had 75% recall. Also, the precision of the text-word strategy was 34.4%, while the precision of the MeSH-term strategy was 47.7%. Therefore, the MeSH-term search strategy yielded both greater recall and greater precision. Conclusions: This study demonstrates the effectiveness of text-word and MeSH s earch strategies on precision and recall. 1996 Jan 13;312(7023):71–2.
